Pre-Trip Intel · Day 1

Provisioning, per Chris.

Your host laid out the full grocery map. The big move: stop in Bozeman on Wednesday before driving south. Once you're in Island Park, options thin out fast.

"If you are driving from Bozeman, MT you can stop at either Costco or Walmart to get your groceries, this would be the least expensive option. I also highly recommend the Daniels Gourmet Meats and Sausage in Bozeman as a butcher shop." — Chris Mehr, Host
Best Value · Day 1

Costco / Walmart — Bozeman Costco ↗ Walmart ↗

★ Cheapest · Stock up on arrival

Chris's #1 pick. Hit either after landing at BZN, before driving south. Lowest prices on the route — you'll never need a major grocery run again.

Specialty · Day 1

Daniels Gourmet Meats & Sausage ↗ Map

▲ Highly recommended · Bozeman butcher

A specific Chris callout. If you plan to grill or cook proper steaks at the cabin, swing through here on your way out of Bozeman.

Closest to Cabin

Sam's Patch ↗ Map

● Closest grocery to property

Small store, has almost everything — fruits, meat, vegetables. The bail-out for the forgotten salt or the 9 PM beer run.

Full Service

The Market Place — West Yellowstone ↗ Map

● Larger · Deli + beer/wine/liquor

Big store, full selection — the only nearby spot for liquor. Prices slightly higher than anywhere else, but it has everything.

If you go south

Walmart Supercenter — Rexburg, ID ↗ Map

○ Mid-trip stop if approaching from the south

Useful if you're returning via the south or want a big-box run mid-trip. Full Walmart selection — fuel, supplies, anything forgotten at the cabin.

The Itinerary

Five days, three big ones, all inside the caldera.

Two travel days bracket three full park days. Geysers Thursday, Canyon Friday, Mammoth & Lamar Saturday — the spine of the trip.

Day 1 · Arrival
Wed · June 3
i.
AUS → BZN → Island Park
Touchdown & the long drive south.
UA 361 → DEN → UA 348 → BZN · grab rental · drive to Costco/Walmart · sweep Daniels Meats · ~2hr drive south · check-in 4:00 PM+

First-day mission: provisioning. The whole week's groceries get loaded in Bozeman because nothing south of here is cheaper. Then the haul south through Big Sky country — about 2 hours via West Yellowstone to Island Park. Settle into the cabin by dinner. Don't push for any park activity tonight — get there, unpack, eat well, sleep early.

Day 2 · Geyser Day
Thu · June 4
ii.
Island Park → West Gate → Old Faithful
Old Faithful, Grand Prismatic, the postcards.
Leave Airbnb ~7:00 AM · West Gate · Old Faithful eruption · Upper Geyser Basin · noon Midway/Grand Prismatic · Fairy Falls overlook · back by dinner

Easiest day, geographically. Island Park is closer to the West Entrance than anywhere else on this trip — use that advantage. Check the predicted eruption window at the Old Faithful visitor center first, then walk the Upper Geyser Basin boardwalks. After lunch, drive 8 miles north to Midway Geyser Basin and hike up the Fairy Falls trail for the elevated Grand Prismatic overlook — that's the shot everyone wants.

Old Faithful Upper Geyser Basin Midway Basin Grand Prismatic Overlook Biscuit Basin
Hour by Hour
7:00 AM
Leave cabin. Beat the crowds into the park. Bring coffee from the cabin.
7:30 AM
West Entrance. Show annual pass or pay fee.
8:30 AM
Old Faithful Visitor Center. Check the eruption prediction board and schedule your walk around the next window.
Eruptions every ~90 min. Show lasts ~4 min. Don't miss it.
9:00 AM
Upper Geyser Basin boardwalk. Walk the 1.5-mi loop: Castle Geyser, Morning Glory Pool, Riverside Geyser. Densest geyser concentration on Earth.
11:00 AM
Biscuit Basin. Short boardwalk, far fewer crowds. Sapphire Pool is electric blue.
12:30 PM
Lunch. Old Faithful Inn cafeteria or packed lunch at a picnic area.
1:30 PM
Midway Geyser Basin. Grand Prismatic Spring boardwalk — rainbow rings of vivid color. Biggest hot spring in the US.
2:30 PM
Fairy Falls overlook hike. 1-mile trail from the trailhead to the elevated Grand Prismatic view — the shot everyone tries to get.
Trailhead: pullout on Fountain Flat Dr, 1 mi south of Midway.
4:30 PM
Drive back to West Entrance.
5:30 PM
Back at cabin. Cook dinner with the Daniels Meats steaks tonight.
Day 3 · Canyon & Wildlife
Fri · June 5
iii.
Island Park → Canyon → Hayden Valley
The Grand Canyon — of the Yellowstone.
Leave 6:30 AM · West Gate · Norris Geyser Basin (quick stop) · 10 AM Canyon Village · Artist Point · Hayden Valley wildlife · back late

Today's longer drive day — about 2 hours each way from Island Park. The reward: the 308-foot Lower Falls dropping into the yellow-walled canyon. Hit Artist Point first for the iconic view, walk the South Rim trail, then loop south through Hayden Valley for bison, elk, and (with luck) bears — the park's other great wildlife corridor outside Lamar.

Norris Geyser Basin Artist Point Lower Falls South Rim Trail Hayden Valley Mud Volcano
Hour by Hour
6:30 AM
Leave cabin. Longer drive today — build in time for canyon crowds.
8:00 AM
Norris Geyser Basin · 30–45 min. Home of Steamboat Geyser (world's tallest active geyser). Back Basin loop is worth the stop.
Skip if running late — Canyon is the priority.
9:30 AM
Canyon Village Visitor Center. Orientation and South Rim Road orientation.
10:00 AM
Artist Point. The iconic overlook — 308-ft Lower Falls crashing into the yellow-walled canyon.
Arrive early. Parking fills by 10:30 AM in peak season.
11:00 AM
Inspiration Point (North Rim). Different angle on the canyon and falls. 10-min drive across.
12:30 PM
Lunch. Canyon Lodge or packed lunch at a picnic spot.
1:30 PM
Hayden Valley. The park's premier wildlife corridor. Slow-roll every pullout: bison herds, sandhill cranes, grizzlies, elk.
Midday sightings are still solid in June — light is good for photography too.
3:00 PM
Mud Volcano area. Dragon's Mouth Spring, Mud Caldron. Sulfuric and weird — a quick 30-min loop.
4:30 PM
Drive back. Norris → Madison → West Entrance.
7:30 PM
Back at cabin. Long day — keep dinner simple.
Day 4 · Mammoth & Lamar
Sat · June 6
iv.
Island Park → Mammoth → Lamar Valley
Terraces, wolves, and the whole north.
Leave 7:00 AM · West Gate · Norris · Mammoth terraces ~9:30 AM · Tower Junction · Lamar Valley noon–4 PM · back by 8 PM

The northern loop — the wildest stretch in the park. Mammoth Hot Springs terraces are unlike anything on Geyser Day: active travertine formations still growing, bone-white and steaming. Then head east to Lamar Valley — Yellowstone's Serengeti — where bison herds are massive in June and wolf packs are spotted more reliably here than anywhere in the lower 48. Bring binoculars. No rushing.

Early start ☀ Mammoth Terraces Tower Falls Lamar Valley · wildlife Wolf & bison country
Hour by Hour
7:00 AM
Leave cabin. The northern loop is the longest day. Pack binoculars — non-optional in Lamar.
7:30 AM
West Entrance → Norris. Drive northeast through Madison. Norris is a pass-through today.
9:00 AM
Mammoth Hot Springs · Lower Terraces. Boardwalk through active travertine: Minerva Terrace, Palette Spring, Liberty Cap. Still growing, still steaming.
Elk are often literally in the parking lot at Mammoth. Don't approach them.
10:00 AM
Upper Terraces drive loop. Drive-through with pullouts — quieter than the lower walk with different geological layers.
11:00 AM
Drive east → Tower Junction. 30-min drive through open sagebrush. Watch for pronghorn on the hillsides.
11:30 AM
Tower Falls. 132-ft waterfall, 5-min walk from parking. Quick and beautiful — don't skip it.
12:00 PM
Enter Lamar Valley. Drive slowly east. Stop at every pullout. This is Yellowstone's Serengeti.
June = bison calving season — look for orange "red dog" calves alongside the herds.
1–4:00 PM
Wolf-watch. Hitching Post and Confluence Overlook pullouts are the classic spots. Join the scope-watchers — they know where the packs are.
No guarantees, but this is the single best place for wolf sightings in the lower 48.
4:00 PM
Turn around at Slough Creek. Head back west through Tower, Norris, Madison.
8:00 PM
Back at cabin. Pack bags tonight. Departure is 8:30 AM — do not leave this for the morning.

Field Notes

Six things worth knowing.

☉
Early start, every day

Wildlife is most active at dawn & dusk. Crowds peak at all the famous spots between 10am–4pm. On Thu/Fri/Sat: be in the park by 7:30 AM.

$
Get the annual pass

Yellowstone alone is $35/vehicle for 7 days. The $80 America the Beautiful annual pass covers Yellowstone, Tetons & every national park — pays for itself this trip alone.

℃
June weather

Daytime 60–75°F, nights drop to 30s. Layers, rain shell, sun hat. Snow still possible at higher elevations (Signal Mountain summit, parts of Tetons).

⊕
No cell signal

Service is patchy at best inside the park. Download offline Google Maps + the NPS app before leaving Bozeman. Set meet-up points before the group splits.

⚐
Bear country

Both parks are grizzly habitat. Carry bear spray on every hike (buy or rent in West Yellowstone, $40–50). Make noise on trails, don't store food in tents.

⁕
Fuel up early

Gas inside the park is limited and pricey. Top off in Island Park or West Yellowstone every morning before heading in. Always more than half-tank at sunset.

— see you in Austin —
